encodeFilter.markdownDescription:
The condition under which each forwarder's output stream compacts an event with encode()

Resolved once by the customer-facing config.yaml from the Receiver's mode options, so every reader of the condition sees the same one:  - **receive mode** (default) and **outputOffload**: `false`, no event is compacted - **receiverOptimize**: `true`, every event is compacted - **compactReceiverLookupFile**: `shouldEncode()`, the cap file's per-pattern decision - **outputSoftDrop**: `!isRoute("tier_down") && !isRoute("offload") && (isRoute("compact") || <decide>)`, where `<decide>` is   one of the three above; the `tier_down` and `offload` slices stay full text  `outputEncodeField` compacts the events the condition holds for, and the Receiver's `compact_events` aggregator counts them. (Default: false)

encodeField.markdownDescription:
The single field expression each forwarder's output stream writes per event

Resolved once by the customer-facing config.yaml as `encoded=(<outputEncodeFilter>) ? encode(...) : fullText(...)`. The offload and soft-drop modes add the `routeState` field to both calls, and `symbolMessageHashField` adds the pattern hash field.  Advanced users can override directly to customize the output field expression. (Default: fullText)

writeTemplates.markdownDescription:
Whether the forwarder emits new TenXTemplates alongside encoded events

True for encoding modes (compact-all, compact-lookup) so decoders can reconstruct events from templateHash + vars. False for receive mode (no encoding → no templates needed). (Default: false)

softDrop.markdownDescription: Write every event with its routeState field and compact the events the regulator marks compact (Accepts boolean or string with $= prefix for runtime evaluation)

offload.markdownDescription: Write every event as full text with its routeState field (Accepts boolean or string with $= prefix for runtime evaluation)

dropFilter.markdownDescription:
The filter expression each output stream uses to decide whether a marked object is written

Events the regulator marks `drop` are left out by default. Set `outputSoftDrop` or `outputOffload` to `true` to write every event with its `routeState` field, for the forwarder to route on. `outputSoftDrop` also compacts the events marked `compact`; `outputOffload` writes every event as full text. (Default: isObject && !isRoute("drop"))

receiverReadOnly.markdownDescription:
Read-only mode, receive events, emit metrics, do not write back to the forwarder

When true, the return output each forwarder input opens (Forward for Fluent Bit, Fluentd and Vector, Unix socket for Filebeat, TCP socket for Logstash, OTLP for the OpenTelemetry Collector) is not constructed, so no event and no template is written back to the forwarder; the aggregators still run and publish their metrics.  The [Reporter](https://doc.log10x.com/apps/reporter/) sets it to `true`. With the [Receiver](https://doc.log10x.com/apps/receiver/) it defaults to `false`. Declared here so that it is accepted as a launch argument or a configuration key with any app that loads a forwarder input; the Receiver and Reporter apps declare it with the same name, type and default. (Accepts boolean or string with $= prefix for runtime evaluation) (Default: false)

limit.markdownDescription:
The most bytes a forwarder input reads in each forwarderInputBytesInterval, 0 for no limit

The most bytes a forwarder input (Fluent Bit, Fluentd, Vector, Filebeat, Logstash, OpenTelemetry Collector) reads from its socket in each `forwarderInputBytesInterval`, such as `20MB`. When the limit is reached, the input stops reading until the interval ends, and the forwarder holds the events in its own buffer meanwhile; no event is dropped.  The default is `2MB` a second. `0` sets no byte limit: the input then stops reading only when the pipeline holds as many events as `objectLimitMaxInstances` allows (by default 5,000 for each 100 MB of heap).  Raise it to let one Receiver take more than 2 MB a second, for example `forwarderInputBytesLimit 20MB`. (Default: 2MB)

interval.markdownDescription:
The interval forwarderInputBytesLimit counts bytes over

The interval over which `forwarderInputBytesLimit` counts the bytes a forwarder input reads, such as `1s` (the default) or `1m`. Has no effect while `forwarderInputBytesLimit` is `0`. (Default: 1s)
